## Summary

**Root cause (diagnosis):** promotion was being treated as a point-in-time state flip instead of a committed configuration transition. That produces four failure modes: promoting a transiently-caught-up learner, overlapping config changes creating disjoint quorums, counting an uncommitted promoted voter toward a lease so a step-down can serve a stale `ReadIndex`, and a snapshot rewind leaving a lagging member marked as a voter.

**Fix (`raftlearner/tracker.go`):**
- **Catch-up gate** — `MaybeCommit` advances commit via a real quorum and samples each learner; `true` iff `commit − match ≤ MaxLag`. Promotion requires `WindowSize` consecutive all-true samples.
- **Single config-change slot** — `pending` serializes `promote`/`joint`/`finalize`; promotions are refused while a change is pending or while `joint` is active.
- **Joint quorum correctness** — reserving `C_old,new` does not change the active voter set; joint commit uses `majority(old) AND majority(new)`; unknown members get learner progress only.
- **Lease fencing** — `ReadIndex` captures `(term, commitIndex)` under a valid lease; `ConfirmRead` re-validates leader/term/lease; `StepDown` invalidates the lease, drops the pending change, and clears all catch-up windows.
- **Snapshot rewind** — `OnSnapshotInstall` clears the window and immediately demotes a voter back to learner when `lastIncluded < match`.

**Verification:** 11 deterministic tests cover lag spikes, partition heal, joint-config refusal, premature-quorum prevention, quorum resize after promotion, step-down/lease-expiry fencing, and snapshot rewind demotion. All pass with `go test -race` (77% statement coverage). I also extracted the three `go` code blocks from the markdown into a fresh directory and confirmed `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, and `go test -race` all succeed — so the document is genuinely self-contained.
